children: shares plunged nearly 15% Thursday morning as investors reacted to an earnings shortfall and concerns about future growth, overshadowing a modest revenue beat.

The software company reported third-quarter revenue of $4.106 billion, up 20.5% from a year earlier and slightly above analyst expectations of $4.09 billion. Earnings under generally accepted accounting principles reached $0.27 per share, missing Wall Street's forecast of $0.35.

Contracted revenue also offered a mixed picture. Current remaining performance obligations, which measure revenue expected from existing contracts over the next 12 months, rose 20.5% to $13.65 billion. However, the company's fourth-quarter forecast for this metric pointed to growth of 18.5%, below analysts' estimate of 19.8%.
ServiceNow raised its full-year 2026 subscription revenue outlook to a range of $15.78 billion to $15.79 billion. It also increased its projected free cash flow margin to 36%.

Despite the higher annual targets, the sharp share-price decline suggests investors remain concerned about the pace of enterprise software growth and spending on artificial intelligence. The next test will be whether ServiceNow can sustain demand and meet its forward targets.

title: ServiceNow Stock Suffers Brutal Selloff After Earnings Miss
